title: The Covenant Promised in Jeremiah 31
lead: The promise in Jeremiah 31:31-34 that God would make a new covenant with Israel and Judah, writing his law on their hearts and forgiving their sin. The New Testament says it is made in the blood of Jesus (Luke 22:20; 1 Corinthians 11:25), and Paul and Hebrews compare it with the covenant of Moses. How the covenant of Jeremiah relates to the covenant of Moses (replacement, renewal, fulfillment) divides Christians and is read differently in Jewish teaching.

sections.h: The promise to Israel and Judah
sections.b: Jeremiah speaks to a people whose covenant had been broken. The new covenant is not a new law but a new way of keeping it: God's instruction written inside, a knowledge of God that needs no teacher, and sin remembered no more. Ezekiel promises something close: a new heart and God's Spirit inside the people (Ezekiel 36:26-27).

Paul names the new covenant at the Lord's Supper and in 2 Corinthians 3, where he contrasts the ministry of Moses with the ministry of the Spirit. Hebrews 8 quotes Jeremiah in full and says the first covenant is "obsolete." Christian traditions read these differently, and Jewish readers have usually seen Jeremiah's promise as the same Torah renewed.
